document.lead: You should spend about 40 minutes on this task.
after: Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

text: It is undeniable that screens now occupy a significant part of many children's daily lives. This trend has clear causes, and although devices can offer genuine educational value, I believe that the negative effects of excessive use currently outweigh the benefits.

Several factors explain this pattern. Firstly, devices have become cheap and widely available, so even young children often have their own tablet or access to their parents' phones. Secondly, many parents use screens as a convenient way to keep children occupied while they cook or work, particularly in households where both adults have demanding jobs. Finally, the content itself is designed to be highly engaging, with games and videos that reward constant attention, making it hard for children to stop. Furthermore, the pandemic made many families rely on devices for school and entertainment, and these habits have often continued.

Screens are not entirely harmful. Educational applications can teach reading, mathematics and languages in an interactive way, and video calls enable children to maintain relationships with relatives who live far away. Moreover, familiarity with technology is a useful skill in a world where most jobs require digital literacy. For children with special needs, specially designed software can also offer support that is difficult to provide in a traditional classroom.

Nevertheless, excessive screen time carries significant risks. Children who spend hours in front of a display are less physically active, which contributes to obesity, and they sleep worse, especially if they use devices before bedtime. It can also reduce face-to-face interaction, which is essential for developing social and emotional skills. Therefore, I would argue that parents and schools should set clear limits, such as no devices at meals or in bedrooms, so that technology serves children rather than controlling them.

document.title: Children and screens
document.question:
Many children today spend several hours a day using screens such as phones, tablets and computers.

Why is this the case? Is it a positive or negative development?
